learning_outcomes.text: Students will acquire fundamental knowledge to perform necessary calculations for creating basic technical projects of high and low voltage electrical installations, while also enabling them to continue studying this type of installations in the future through a process of permanent updating.
They will know the constituent parts of electrical installations in buildings and the basic criteria for their design and calculation.
They will become aware of the importance of designing electrical installations with safety criteria.
They will acquire the necessary skill to handle technical specifications from manufacturer catalogs, as well as mandatory regulations and standards.

They will obtain fundamental knowledge to carry out the calculation of energy installations for domestic hot water (DHW), heating, and air conditioning, as well as establish the basis for continuous learning regarding these installations.
They will know and be able to design energy installations and their component equipment, adhering to relevant regulations and seeking energy efficiency.
They will acquire knowledge related to environmental impact, installation safety, and energy audits.

syllabus_topics: Generalities.
Electric power system (EPS). Parts and diagrams of an electrical installation. AT and BT regulations. AT installations.
Connection of basic circuits. Symbology and single-line diagram of circuits.
Power forecast.
Power forecast: ITC-BT 10 and ITC-BT 25. Commercial and industrial installations. ITC-BT 19. Distribution by panels. Coefficients.
Design and calculation of electrical conduits.
Electrical conductor. Parts of an electrical cable. Designation. Calculation of the conductor core section. Conduits.
Checking the behavior of a cable by temperature and voltage drop.
Start of an electrical project. Calculation of power forecast and cable section of a basic electrical installation.
Protection in electrical installations.
Purpose of protection. Installation protections. Personal protection.
Assembly of a basic electrical panel.
Problem solving. Basic building project.
Basic concepts of Thermal Engineering in thermal installations.
Heat generation. Combustion. Fuels.
Thermal Insulation. Energy Efficiency in Buildings.
Mixed transmission. Surface insulation. Critical Radius. Thermal insulation. Economic insulation. Energy efficiency. CTE.
Calculation and design of surface insulation.
Heating and DHW Installations and Equipment.
Heating installations. Calculation of heating thermal loads. Sizing of heating and DHW installations. Application of CTE and RITE.
Sizing of a DHW installation by solar energy.
Calculation of a heating installation. Estimation of heating thermal loads for a dwelling.
Cold Production. Refrigeration Systems.

Cold production. Cold production procedures. Mechanical vapor compression system. Multiple compression systems. Absorption system. Energy comparison of mechanical refrigeration and absorption systems.
Calculation of a refrigeration installation.
Air Conditioning Installations and Equipment.

Psychrometry. Psychrometric chart. Psychrometric processes. General study of an air conditioning installation. Air conditioning evolution cycle. Interior design conditions. Exterior conditions. Calculation of required air flow and air conditioner power. Application of CTE and RITE.
Calculation of sizing of an Air Conditioning installation. Estimation of Thermal Loads.
Calculation of a thermal installation in a building. Different configurations.
teaching_methods: Seminar or problem-solving activities in class
Personal study, individual or group work, and bibliography reading

assessment_methods.method: Final theoretical/practical exam and/or cumulative and/or eliminatory partial exams
Practical activities carried out in: classroom, laboratory, computer room, field, visits, etc.
Resolution and delivery of activities (cases, problems, reports, assignments, projects, etc.), individually and/or in groups

assessment_rules: The final grade is based on a numerical score from 0 to 10. The final theoretical/practical exam or partial exams contribute 50%. This exam has two parts, each weighted 25% in the ordinary call if the partial is passed, otherwise the final covers both parts for 50%. Practical activities contribute 10%, and problem-solving and project delivery (challenges) contribute 40%; challenges must be defended to obtain points. To pass, a student must obtain a minimum overall grade of 5, having also achieved a minimum of 3 points in each of the two content blocks (A and B) of the exams. If minimums are not met, the final grade will be the minimum of the total score or 3 points. Practical activities and challenges are non-recoverable for extraordinary calls.
